generation.explanation: A cylinder's volume is base area times height: V = πr²h. A cone with the same base and height holds exactly one third of that — pour three cone-fulls of sand or water into the cylinder and it fills perfectly to the top. The deeper reason: at a fraction t of the way from apex to base, the cone's cross-section has radius t·r, hence area t²·πr²; averaging t² from 0 to 1 gives exactly 1/3, so V_cone = (1/3)πr²h. The animation pours 3 cones into the cylinder, then lets you explore with a slider or by clicking the cone.
